entities.name: streetlights
entities.description: Streetlights are essential for public safety and urban aesthetics. The city uses various types of streetlights, including wood poles, concrete poles, and specialized Denman Fink lights. Many are located in districts such as Coral Gables, French Village, and along major roads like 8th Street (Calle Ocho) and Bird Road. Some streetlights are privately developed but on city right-of-way, and there are ongoing efforts to repair and upgrade them to enhance city branding and urban design.

entities.name: urban design
entities.description: Urban design in the city focuses on aesthetic and functional aspects of public spaces, including street lighting, monuments, and street furniture. It aims to create a cohesive and attractive environment that reflects the city's brand and history, enhancing the experience for residents and visitors alike.

entities.name: branding
entities.description: City branding involves promoting a unique identity through visual elements like street jewelry, monuments, and streetlights. The city seeks to establish a recognizable and appealing image that embodies its history, culture, and community spirit.

entities.name: city identity
entities.description: City identity encompasses the historical, cultural, and aesthetic elements that define the city's character. Efforts include maintaining historical streetlights, monuments, and public art to preserve and promote the city's unique sense of place.
